data.description:
## The defect

`docker_unaccounted_bytes` differences two measurements that are **layout-independent but
UNIT-INCOMMENSURABLE**:

- minuend: `du -sx --block-size=1 /var/lib/docker` — counts **ALLOCATED BLOCKS**
- subtrahend: all four `docker system df` rows — report **APPARENT sizes**

Across 1,879,235 files on 4 KiB xfs blocks that is a **12.4% structural inflation of the minuend**,
and it scales with the Docker root.

The earlier widening fix (overlay2-only -> whole Docker root, partial ledger -> all four rows) was
correct and is not in question. This is a second, independent defect the widening did not address.

## Measured on the host, 2026-09-05

```
docker root bytes=13642739712  overlay2=12604108800  ledger=10957600000  unaccounted=2685139712
```

`du --apparent-size` splits the residue cleanly, with no double counting:

| Component | Bytes | Share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| xfs block-allocation overhead (allocated 13,642,739,712 − apparent 12,140,814,875) | **1,501,924,837** | **56%** |
| Real content no ledger row covers (apparent 12,140,814,875 − ledger 10,957,600,000) | **1,183,214,875** | **44%** |
| Sum | 2,685,139,712 | exact |

The un-ledgered content, by subtree: `buildkit` 65.3 MB, `image` 28.8 MB, `containers` 282 KB,
`volumes` ~12 MB block overhead, network/misc ~82 KB — **~94.5 MB, 3.5% of the residue**. The
remaining ~1.09 GB sits inside `overlay2`: of 122 directories, 102 are referenced by
`image/overlay2/layerdb`, and **20 are referenced by neither cache-id nor mount-id, totalling
1,012,375,552 bytes**, every one with an mtime between 2026-09-02 08:45 and 2026-09-03 06:38 — the
outage window. Static wreckage, not an active leak.

## Why the threshold must NOT be raised

The 2 GiB threshold was set from the incident narrative rather than a baseline, and the code comment
says so in its own words: *"far above that overhead (hundreds of MB on this box)"*. **The measured
overhead is 1.50 GB, not hundreds of MB** — 70% of the threshold is consumed by an artifact before
a single orphaned byte is counted.

Projecting against this host's own configured 20 GiB Docker budget: **block overhead alone reaches
2 GiB at roughly 18 GiB of Docker root, so the alarm fires from rounding before the box reaches its
own cap.** That is a guaranteed future false positive, not a hypothetical.

Raising the threshold would preserve the units bug AND blunt sensitivity to the orphan class the
alarm just correctly detected. Fix the units instead.

## Fix

Change the residue's minuend ONLY to `du -sx --apparent-size --block-size=1 /var/lib/docker`.
Today's residue then reads **1,183,214,875 B (1.10 GiB)** — under threshold, and composed almost
entirely of the ~1.0 GB of genuine orphans, which is what the metric exists to surface.

**Leave `docker_storage_bytes` on ALLOCATED blocks.** That metric should report real disk
consumption; only the DIFFERENCE needs commensurable sides. Changing both would be the wrong fix.

Keep the threshold at 2 GiB: post-fix it sits ~1.8x above the current genuine residue and would
still have caught the 6.5 GB 2026-09-02 event with large margin.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 - The residue's minuend uses apparent size, so both sides of the subtraction are in the
      same units. `docker_storage_bytes` remains on allocated blocks.
- [ ] AC2 - Defect-seeded against real numbers: a test replays this host's measured values
      (allocated 13,642,739,712 / apparent 12,140,814,875 / ledger 10,957,600,000) and asserts the
      residue is 1,183,214,875 — and FAILS against the allocated-blocks minuend, which yields
      2,685,139,712. A test that cannot tell the two apart does not pin this.
- [ ] AC3 - The threshold's justification is recorded against a MEASURED baseline rather than a
      narrative estimate. The existing comment's "hundreds of MB" claim is corrected — it was wrong
      by an order of magnitude and is what made the threshold look safe.
- [ ] AC4 - The runbook's "where the unaccounted bytes usually are" subtree list is corrected: its
      three named candidates account for 3.5% here. Container JSON logs are 282 KB total, because
      every compose service logs to journald rather than `json-file`.

## Non-goals

Not reverting the layout-independence widening — that fix was right and is what makes the metric
survive the containerd snapshotter. Not raising the threshold. Not reclaiming the orphaned bytes,
which is an operator action.

## Related operational finding (not part of this fix)

`/etc/docker/daemon.json` mtime `2026-09-05 01:01:06 UTC`, `dockerd` started `2026-09-04 22:07:34
UTC` — so the 5 GiB `builder.gc maxUsedSpace` cap is **installed but NOT in effect**, and Build
Cache is already **5.433 GB, over that cap**. A single scheduled `systemctl restart docker` both
puts the cap in force AND sweeps the ~1.0 GB of orphaned overlay2 (standard overlay2 startup
behaviour). One restart, both problems.

Separately: `DOCKER_DF_TIMEOUT` defaults to 20 s, and a probe run exceeded it under concurrent load
and returned empty, succeeding at 90 s. A failed ledger read publishes nothing, and
`treat_missing_data = "breaching"` then pages. Thin margin on a contended box; low-confidence
observation, recorded rather than acted on.
data.title: docker_unaccounted_bytes subtracts apparent-size ledger rows from an allocated-blocks du, so 56% of today's 2.5 GiB residue is xfs block overhead and the alarm will fire from rounding before the host reaches its own budget
